rubrics.justification: The response overstates image features: the blastocyst appears somewhat collapsed/partially expanded with poorly distinct ICM and TE on this single image, yet it describes a clearly expanded cavity, distinct upper-right ICM, and cohesive uniform TE not convincingly visible.
It integrates age, prior biochemical pregnancies, ovarian reserve, BMI, sperm parameters, and endometrium well with embryo quality, though some links are somewhat speculative.

Overall logic is structured and consistent, especially around age-related aneuploidy and prior biochemical losses, but some probability framing and morphology-based confidence are stronger than the image supports.

Much is broadly IVF-consistent, but several recommendations are not strongly guideline-based or are controversial for this scenario (routine thrombophilia testing beyond APS, ERA, NK-cell testing, empiric LMWH/intralipids/IVIG, MTHFR).
Provides clear next-step recommendations for transfer monitoring, luteal support review, and future cycle planning, though some suggested tests/interventions may not be appropriate routinely.
